reference.title: Barbell Rollout
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Brace before rolling out, breathe out slowly on the way out or hold the brace, breathe in once back at the start.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s out, a short hold, about 1.8 s back

prescription.tempo: 2 s out, short hold, 2 s back
prescription.load: Bodyweight plus range: roll only as far as the low back stays flat (no sag). Light round plates (standard 45 cm) let the bar roll smoothly.
prescription.progression: Roll out further each week, then pause at the far point; standing rollouts are the advanced step.

cues.text: Kneel on a mat, knees under the hips, bar on its plates on the floor under the shoulders, overhand grip about shoulder width, arms straight. Tuck the pelvis slightly and brace.
Roll the bar forward on its plates, letting the hips and shoulders travel forward together; the arms reach overhead and the body lowers in one line from knees to shoulders.
Stop just before the low back starts to sag; ribs down, glutes tight.
Pull the bar back toward the knees with straight arms, bracing the abs, until the hips are back over the knees.

mistakes.mistake: Low back sagging at the far point
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range; keep the ribs down and the pelvis slightly tucked.

mistakes.mistake: Hips staying back (only the arms move)
mistakes.fix: Let the hips travel forward with the bar so the body lengthens as one piece.
Keep the arms straight; the shoulders and abs do the work.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling back by piking the hips first
mistakes.fix: Pull the bar back with the abs and lats; the hips follow.

kinematics.norm: Trunk lowers toward level as the bar rolls out (clinical opinion); rollouts were among the most demanding exercises for the rectus abdominis and obliques (Escamilla 2006)
From flexed hips over the knees to near straight hips at the far point (clinical opinion)
Arms move from under the shoulders to overhead in line with the trunk (clinical opinion)
Plates roll on the floor the whole rep (common coaching)
Slow, controlled out and back (clinical opinion); core exercise reviews favour controlled anti-extension work (Oliva-Lozano 2020)

cautions: Low-back pain or a sagging low back: shorten the range; keep the spine neutral (McGill 1998).
Use round plates of equal size so the bar rolls straight; a mat protects the knees.
Shoulder pain overhead: stop the roll earlier.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shorter range, or roll up a slight incline / toward a wall that stops the bar.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis resists the trunk extending as the lever lengthens (Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist extension and keep the pelvis tucked (Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist extension and keep the pelvis tucked (Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar back from overhead and control the roll out.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar back from overhead and control the roll out.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Long head helps hold and pull the straight arms.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Long head helps hold and pull the straight arms.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Controls the shoulder flexion as the arms reach overhead.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Controls the shoulder flexion as the arms reach overhead.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Work with the hips flexing on the way back.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Work with the hips flexing on the way back.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the ribs.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the ribs.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Helps pull the arms back down from overhead.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Helps pull the arms back down from overhead.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Keeps the hips extended at the far point.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Keeps the hips extended at the far point.
